steps.prompt_exact: Make me a one-file offline mobile browser tool for freelancers where I paste a client project brief, tag the risk clues I notice, and it turns that into a red/yellow/green proposal fit heatmap with follow-up questions, price-pressure warnings, and a copyable go/no-go summary.

Now let me think through the design and build this tool.

Design plan:

This is a tool for freelancers — cynical, experienced, time-pressed people who've been burned by scope creep and bad clients. The aesthetic should feel like a well-worn professional instrument, not a cute startup app. Think: a legal pad meets a terminal readout. Dark slate background, sharp monospace accents for the heatmap cells, a warm amber for warnings, with data-dense but breathable layout.

Palette: 
#1a1d23 bg, 
#f0ede6 text, 
#e8c84a amber warnings, 
#4caf72 green, 
#e05a3a red, 
#f0b429 yellow, 
#2d3240 card surface
Type: System monospace for scores/tags, system sans-serif for body — no Google Fonts, works offline
Signature: The heatmap cells animate in like a score being revealed — each category flips from neutral to its risk color with a brief delay cascade
Layout: Three-column desktop, single column mobile — paste zone top, tag cloud middle, heatmap + outputs bottom
Created a file, read a file
Created a file, read a file

BriefCheck — save it to your phone, open it locally, works 100% offline.

Here's what it does end-to-end:

Paste → auto-scan. Drop a brief in the text area and hit Analyze. The tool scans the text for ~12 risk patterns (regex-matched) — things like "ASAP," "unlimited revisions," "previous freelancer," net-90 payment language, and vague scope signals — and auto-fires the relevant tags so you don't have to do all the work manually.

Tag layer. 17 preset risk clues in red/yellow/green — tap to toggle. Add your own custom clues with severity. Everything stacks.

Heatmap. Six categories scored 0–100 with a cascade reveal animation: Scope Clarity, Budget Health, Timeline Risk, Client Quality, Payment Safety, Legal/IP Risk. Color-coded cells, overall score bar up top.

Follow-up questions panel — generated from your active tags. Up to 7 targeted questions you can drop into a reply email before quoting.

Price-pressure warnings — plain-English contractor advice: "Deferred payment = free credit. Require 30–50% upfront." Stuff that's easy to forget when you want the work.

Go/No-Go summary — copyable plaintext block with verdict (GO / CAUTION / NO-GO), category breakdown, flag list, and a one-paragraph recommendation you can paste into a Notion doc or send yourself.

The syntax errors are on lines 856, 858, and 883 — curly apostrophes (') inside single-quoted JS strings ('What's...', 'What's...', 'can you share more context...). Also need to eliminate all innerHTML, onclick/onkeydown attributes, and template-literal HTML injection. Rewriting the whole file cleanly.

Ran 6 commands
Ran 6 commands

All checks pass.

Presented file
Presented file

Here's what was fixed and why each change was made:

Syntax errors — the original file had curly/smart apostrophes (U+2019) inside plain single-quoted JS strings on three lines: 'What's the approved budget...', 'What's the hard deadline...', and 'can you share more context...'. JavaScript's parser treats those as string terminators, which is what produced the "missing ) after argument list" error. All strings are now written with straight quotes or rephrased to avoid apostrophes entirely.

No more innerHTML with dynamic content — every list, chip, heatmap cell, and panel is now built with createElement, createTextNode, appendChild, and textContent only. User-pasted brief text and custom tag labels are only ever assigned to .textContent, never injected as markup.

No more inline handlers — onclick, onkeydown, oninput attributes are completely gone from the HTML. Every event is attached in JS via addEventListener after the DOM is ready, with closures properly capturing tag IDs for the remove buttons.

Verified by Node.js — ran a programmatic check confirming: JS syntax valid, no inline handlers in HTML, no innerHTML= in the script block, no smart quotes anywhere.
